title: The Mayans Ran Out of Stone, Not Time

slides.title: Apocalyptic Predictions and the 2012 Myth
slides.subtitle: Why the Mayan calendar end sparked false doomsday fears

points: Apocalyptic forecasts have repeatedly failed throughout history, yet persist in popular culture
Mayan calendars recorded days, years, and 5‑millennium cycles extending far beyond their era
Modern new‑age groups claim the calendar stopped because the world ends
In reality the calendar simply ran out of stone for further inscriptions

bullets.citedChunkText: History has a long and rich tradition of apocalyptic predictions – all of which were wrong – yet some people still think that this time ’round in 2012 is the real deal. Why 2012? Because of ancient Mayan calendars. Obviously. Mayan calendars not only recorded the days and years, but also longer cycles of about 5 Millennia. So they could easily make calendars that went 1,000s of years into the future. But, of course, 1,000s of years in the future from 1,000s of years ago brings us to current times when the Mayan calendars stop in 2012. slides.title: Mass Hysteria and NASA’s Response
slides.subtitle: From fringe belief to mainstream panic and official clarification

points: 2012 disaster movies and Emmy‑nominated documentaries fueled public fear
The History Channel’s apocalyptic specials turned fringe belief into mass hysteria
NASA diverted resources to answer endless public queries about 2012
Issued a webpage stating Mayans lacked modern scientific knowledge and did not predict an end

And because new agers are happy – though scientifically illiterate – people their vision of 2012 was a great spiritual awakening or world reboot or other hippy-consciousness-expanding nonsense that the Mayans, who spent time puling strings of thorns through peoples’ tongue, probably didn’t have in mind. To a normal person the thought that: calendar finishes therefore end of the world is an odd conclusion to draw. After all, the amount of time in the Universe is infinite and the amount of stone is limited. So, at some point the Mayans had to stop carving calendars. But never mind. What should have stayed a fringe belief turned into mass hysteria with the 2012 disaster

slides.title: Impossible Predictions vs. Mayan Reality
slides.subtitle: Why the Mayans never forecasted an apocalypse

points: Geomagnetic reversal, Planet X collision, local supernova, alien invasion, unknown beam
All claims lack scientific evidence and ignore geological timescales
Mayans could not predict distant astrophysical events or the Spanish conquest
Only non‑Mayan sources falsely attributed apocalypse predictions to them

But the parade of crazy marched on anyway making wilder and wilder predictions for Earth
